source.title: DART: Mitigating Harm Drift in Difference-Aware LLMs via Distill-Audit-Repair Training
source.authors: Ziwen Pan; Zihan Liang; Jad Kabbara; Ali Emami

record.tranche_reason: The study discusses safety alignment and reports its own fine-tuning-related changes in rationale toxicity and refusal/abstention. Its task is difference-awareness classification, however; it does not test harmful-request compliance after harmful or ordinary benign instruction fine-tuning, response-position KL, opening-token bypasses, safety localization in weights, or deepening safety.
record.gate_note: The study’s own rationale-toxicity, harm-drift, refusal, and abstention results are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"]. They measure explanatory harm or response engagement in difference-awareness and external benchmark settings, not compliance with harmful user requests or the first-token mechanism. Claims and results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes Llama-3-8B-Instruct on benign difference-awareness rationales and measures rationale toxicity, audited harm drift, and refusal or abstention. It never measures compliance with harmful user requests, which V1 and V2 require. The authors call harm drift distinct from compliance-based safety degradation. It has no per-token KL, prefill or suffix attack, weight-localization analysis, or safety-deepening training, so V3–V7 are not tested. The findings are related constructs and belong in fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. Distillation raises accuracy (39.0% to 68.8%) but causes harm drift in rationales. Audit plus severity-weighted repair cuts drift cases by 72.6% while keeping accuracy. Safety did not transfer automatically from teacher to student.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses teacher-generated rationale distillation on 4,800 difference-awareness examples, followed by audited, severity-weighted repair and an optional inference-time explanation policy. It does not use the original harmful-example or benign-instruction fine-tuning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with the inference-time policy, audit judge, and drift-detection threshold. The paper reports that policy-on reduces toxicity, GPT-4 versus DeepSeek-Chat judging gives nearly identical final performance, and threshold choice changes detection precision/recall and the repair pool.

fits_no_version.finding: On Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Stage I distillation on 4,800 benign task examples raised median rationale toxicity by 7.1% (3.81e-5 to 4.08e-5) and produced 435 audited harm-drift cases. Repair cut these to 3.52e-5 and 119 cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign task-specific rationale distillation increases the harmfulness of explanatory content, separate from harmful-request compliance, and targeted repair reduces it.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusals on 280 open-ended difference-awareness queries fell from 34.3% to 3.0%. Abstention on BOLD, HolisticBias, RealToxicityPrompts and HateCheck fell from 22.8% to 0%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DART fine-tuning removes refusal and abstention on demographic-sensitive and hate-containing prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: After DART, hate-classifier scores rose on HateCheck (rrb +0.24) and RealToxicityPrompts (+0.09) while toxicity fell. The authors attribute this mostly to detector brittleness on counter-speech and say 7.8% of the failing subset is truly hateful.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning that removes abstention on hateful prompts yields mixed hate-classifier outcomes, partly from evaluator artifacts.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The paper notes that harm evaluation relies on toxicity classifiers and LLM-as-Judge, which may miss subtle harms or flag appropriate demographic discussion. Stage III repair is transductive: it uses held-out test prompts and their gold labels. The open-ended evaluation is modest in scale, and the study says it lacks a large independently sourced difference-awareness benchmark.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results were left out. Additional subgroup, benchmark, policy, and ablation results concern the same difference-awareness rationale-harm or refusal constructs; the selected rows retain the central reported findings relevant to the claim’s broader safety subject.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful-request examples and no measure of harmful-request compliance.
Benign task fine-tuning is done, but only rationale toxicity, harm drift and refusal on difference-awareness prompts are measured, not harmful-request compliance (e.g., on AdvBench or HEx-PHI).
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL or response-position analysis.
No prefill, adversarial-suffix or decoding-change attacks.
LoRA is used only as a training tool; there is no test of whether safety is localized in few weights or ranks.
The paper speculates that distillation loses implicit safety constraints but does not test why safety is shallow.
Stage III repair reduces rationale harm but is not training that spreads refusal beyond the first tokens, and robustness to attack is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The cross-family results (Table 15), teacher comparison and ablations concern the same rationale-harm construct and do not bear on any version. Stage III repair is transductive: it uses test-set prompts with gold labels given to the teacher.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune on harmful-request examples or measure harmful-request compliance.
Does not test ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction data for harmful-request compliance; its task-specific rationale distillation measures a different outcome.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement or response-position analysis.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial-suffix, or decoding-change bypass test.
LoRA is used for training, but the study does not test whether a small set of parameters or ranks carries safety behaviour.
The study discusses harm drift from its task-specific distillation, but does not test why safety is shallow or whether the data/objective causes first-token shallowness.
No training to spread safety beyond initial response tokens or test of whether such deepening holds up.
